t.5.20.1: Having heard the harsh words of Sītā, the lord of the rākṣasas then replied to Sītā, who was lovely to behold, with words that were unpleasant.
t.5.20.2: The more a man will try to soothe women, the more he falls into their power; the more he will speak pleasing words to them, the more he is scorned.
t.5.20.3: The desire that has arisen in me for you restrains my anger, as a skilled charioteer, having reached the road, reins in galloping horses.
t.5.20.5: For this reason, O fair-faced one, I do not have you put to death, though you deserve death and deserve contempt, you who are devoted to one falsely gone forth as an ascetic.
t.5.20.4: Perverse, they say, is the desire of men: toward whatever person it becomes bound, toward that very person compassion and affection, it is said, arise.
t.5.20.6: For each and every harsh word that you speak to me, O Maithilī, a cruel death would be fitting for you.
t.5.20.7: Having thus spoken to Vaidehī, Rāvaṇa, lord of the Rākṣasas, filled with anger and agitation, then spoke a further reply to Sītā.
t.5.20.8: Two months, the time limit I have set for you, are to be kept by me; after that, O fair-complexioned lady, you shall ascend my bed.
t.5.20.9: But after two months, if you still do not desire me as your husband, the cooks will cut you up in my kitchen for my morning meal.
t.5.20.10: Seeing Jānakī being threatened thus by the lord of the Rākṣasas, those wide-eyed maidens of the Devas and Gandharvas were filled with despair.
t.5.20.11: Some of the women comforted Sītā, who had been threatened by that rākṣasa, with gestures of their lips, and others likewise with their eyes and faces.
t.5.20.13: Surely you have no one who stands firm in your highest good, no one who would restrain you from this blameworthy deed.
t.5.20.12: Comforted by them, Sītā spoke to Rāvaṇa, lord of the Rākṣasas, words that served her own good, proud with the courage of her virtuous conduct.
t.5.20.14: For who in the three worlds other than you would desire, even in his mind, me, the wife of that righteous-souled one, like Śacī, the wife of Śacīpati?
t.5.20.15: O vilest of rākṣasas, you have spoken sinful words to the wife of Rāma, whose splendour is immeasurable; where can you go to escape from him?
t.5.20.16: Just as a proud elephant and a hare may be found together in the forest, so Rāma is regarded as the elephant, and you, O base one, as the hare.
t.5.20.17: You, such as you are, feel no shame here in reviling the lord of the Ikṣvākus; and yet you do not come within the range of his sight.
t.5.20.18: These cruel, hideous, black-and-tawny eyes of yours: why have they not been destroyed and fallen out, as you look upon me with an ignoble gaze?
t.5.20.19: I am the wife of that righteous-souled one and the daughter-in-law of Daśaratha; how is it, O wicked one, that your tongue does not split apart as you speak to me so?
t.5.20.21: I could not have been carried off from that wise Rāma; this has been ordained by fate for your destruction, of that there is no doubt.
t.5.20.20: Only because there is no command from Rāma, and to preserve my austerity, I do not reduce you to ashes, O Daśagrīva, with my fiery power that is capable of turning you to ashes.
t.5.20.22: You are a hero, the brother of Dhanada, and well endowed with forces; why then did you draw Rāma away and commit the theft of his wife?
t.5.20.23: Having heard Sītā's words, Rāvaṇa, lord of the rākṣasas, opened wide his cruel eyes and gazed at Jānakī.
t.5.20.24: Resembling a dark rain-cloud, with mighty arms and a massive neck, glorious, with the strength and gait of a lion, he had a blazing tongue and fierce eyes.
t.5.20.25: Tall, with a crown whose tip was swaying, adorned with bright garlands and fragrant unguents, wearing red garlands and garments, and decked with armlets of burnished gold.
t.5.20.28: Gazing at Vaidehī, his eyes reddened with anger, Rāvaṇa spoke to Sītā, hissing like a serpent.
t.5.20.26: Well girt with a great dark-blue waist-cord, he looked like Mandara bound by the serpent at the churning-forth of the nectar.
t.5.20.30: Having spoken thus to Maithilī, King Rāvaṇa, who makes his enemies cry out, then gave orders to all the rākṣasīs of dreadful appearance.
t.5.20.27: Adorned with a pair of earrings having the hue of the rising sun, he looked like a mountain graced by two aśoka trees with red shoots and blossoms.
t.5.20.29: O you who are devoted to one overtaken by misfortune and bereft of wealth, today I shall destroy you, as the sun with its splendour destroys the twilight.
t.5.20.31: He saw one with a single eye and one with a single ear, and likewise one whose ears served as her cloak; one with cow's ears and one with elephant's ears, one with drooping ears and one with no ears at all.
t.5.20.33: She had an enormous head and neck, enormous breasts and belly, and enormous mouth and eyes; one had a long tongue and another had no tongue at all, one had no nose, and there were others with the face of a lion, the face of a cow, and the face of a sow.
t.5.20.32: There were two with the feet of an elephant and of a horse, and he saw one with the feet of a cow, one with tufts of hair upon her feet, a one-eyed one, a one-footed one, one with broad feet, and one with no feet at all.
t.5.20.34: O rākṣasīs, all of you, gathering together, act quickly so that Sītā, the daughter of Janaka, swiftly comes under my control.
t.5.20.36: Having thus given his commands, the lord of the Rākṣasas, his heart seized by lust and wrath, threatened Jānakī again and again.
t.5.20.35: With measures both harsh and gentle, with conciliation, gifts, sowing discord and the like, and by raising the rod of punishment, he sought to bring Vaidehī round.
t.5.20.37: Then the rākṣasī Dhānyamālinī quickly approached, and, embracing Daśagrīva, spoke these words.
t.5.20.38: Sport with me, great king; what use to you is this Sītā? The body of one who desires a woman who does not desire him is only tormented, but for one who desires a woman who desires him in return, the delight is beautiful.
t.5.20.39: Thus addressed by the rākṣasī, the mighty one, flung upward, then entered the dwelling that shone with the colour of the blazing sun.
t.5.20.40: Then those daughters of the gods and gandharvas, and the daughters of the nāgas, surrounding Daśagrīva, entered that finest of dwellings.
t.5.20.41: Having threatened Maithilī, who stood firm, devoted to dharma, yet trembling, Rāvaṇa, deluded by desire, left Sītā and entered his own radiant palace.
